figures.bridge_line: the governor who became a bishop in a week - and then told an emperor, from inside a besieged basilica, that the emperor is within the Church and not above it

dates.floruit: provincial governor, then bishop of Milan by popular acclamation 374 - elected while still an unbaptized catechumen, baptized and consecrated within about a week (an irregular path remarkable enough to be recorded, not a general rule); the Altar of Victory exchange 384; the basilica standoff 386; Callinicum 388; Thessalonica and the emperor's penance 390

figures.bridge_line: the emperor who ended the empire's hunt for the church and started funding it instead - and whose alliance made a bishop's office a form of power the state had to reckon with

dates.floruit: victor at the Milvian Bridge 312; the Milan agreement 313; convened Nicaea 325; dedicated Constantinople 330

names.name: Constantine I ("the Great", c. 272/273-337, sole emperor 324-337)

figures.bridge_line: Constantine's son, under whom the imperial church itself confessed the Son as "like" the Father - and bishops who refused learned what imperial confession-making cost

dates.floruit: sole emperor 353-361 after defeating Magnentius; the twin councils of 359 and the Homoian settlement of 360 pressed under his authority

names.name: Constantius II (317-361, emperor from 337, sole emperor 353-361)

figures.bridge_line: the bishop who argued Rome's primacy in verse and stone - commissioning poems at the martyrs' graves so that pilgrims could read the see's claim for themselves

dates.born: c. 305 (scholarly convention; Jerome's notice says he died "at the age of almost eighty")
dates.died: 384, "in the reign of the Emperor Theodosius" (Jerome, De Viris 103, verified)
dates.floruit: bishop of Rome 366-384; the martyr-epigram program; the see's self-presentation as guardian of apostolic memory

figures.bridge_line: the historian at the emperor's side - the man who wrote the alliance's own founding story, and hedged, in writing, on the council's defining word

dates.floruit: bishop of Caesarea from c. 313; present and subscribing at Nicaea 325; the alliance's chief literary voice to his death

figures.bridge_line: the bishop of Rome who wrote, a generation before Damasus, as though Rome's review of another church's judgment were ancient custom - this world's own window's earliest surviving voice of the claim (earlier Roman assertions exist outside it - Victor c.190, Stephen 256 - not this world's own material)

dates.floruit: bishop of Rome 337-352; the letter to the Eusebian party (the anti-Nicene faction named for Eusebius of Nicomedia, not Eusebius of Caesarea the historian) 341

figures.bridge_line: the empress who demanded a basilica for the Homoian faith she actually held - and whom the record lets speak only through her enemies

dates.floruit: exercising a mother's dominant influence over the young Valentinian II at Milan - no formal regency title is attested; the Homoian court's principal in the 386 basilica demand

names.name: Justina (d. c. 388), empress, mother and dominant influence over the young Valentinian II

figures.bridge_line: the bishop whose letter went to a council in his place - and was received, by those who received it, as Peter himself still speaking

dates.died: 461 - a decade past this world's own 451 close; his death is outside the window and nothing after Chalcedon's immediate aftermath is this world's to narrate
dates.floruit: bishop of Rome 440-461; the Tome to Flavian 449; Chalcedon and the Canon 28 rejection 451-452

names.name: Leo I ("the Great"), bishop of Rome (440-461)

figures.bridge_line: the emperor who called the council meant to settle everything - the alliance's convening power at the world's own closing scene

dates.floruit: Eastern emperor from 450; with Pulcheria convened Chalcedon 451

figures.bridge_line: the empress the letter Anatolius of Constantinople sent to Leo names alongside Marcian as "most pious and in all respects faithful" when the Definition was laid on Euphemia's altar - one of the two women this world's record shows wielding real power over the church's own settlement

dates.floruit: Augusta 414; with Marcian from 450 the convening power behind Chalcedon 451

names.name: Aelia Pulcheria (399-453), Augusta from 414, empress with Marcian from 450

figures.bridge_line: the emperor who made the Nicene faith the empire's own law - and who, after his soldiers massacred a city, did public penance before a bishop rather than break with him

dates.died: 395; the empire's administration divided between his sons after him
dates.floruit: emperor 379-395; baptized at Thessalonica during illness 380; the "Cunctos populos" law 380; the massacre at Thessalonica and his public penance 390

figures.bridge_line: the Eastern emperor under whom the Homoian confession ruled again - and pro-Nicene bishops went into exile a second time

dates.floruit: Eastern emperor 364-378; the Homoian confession again enforced in the East under his authority
